advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Clamp max_tokens to the MIN published ceiling across all fallback candidates, not just the resolved primary, so a fallback leg to a smaller-ceiling model cannot still receive an oversized ask.
evidence: structured_run.py:291-293: `_ceiling = _known_model_output_ceiling(resolved)` / `if _ceiling is not None: eff_max_tokens = min(eff_max_tokens, _ceiling)` — clamps to the primary only

runner.py:337 `candidates = [resolved]` and runner.py:344-346 build a `FallbackModel` over the whole candidate set, but `build_model_settings(cfg, req, caps, resolved, ...)` (runner.py:423-424) receives only the primary string, and one `model_settings['max_tokens']` is sent for the whole call
model_classes.py:402 `candidates = [resolved, *(_resolve_target(...) for t in targets)]` — a fallback candidate can be a smaller-ceiling model than the primary
advisory.finding: The clamp keys off only the primary model (`resolved`); on a fallback chain the single `max_tokens` is sent to a `FallbackModel` wrapping all candidates, so if the primary's ceiling is 128K but a fallback candidate is a 64K model, the oversized ask still rides into the fallback leg and reproduces the exact Bedrock 400 this fix targets.
scenarios: An operator opts a 128K-primary class into a fallback chain whose fallback target is haiku (64K); the primary is momentarily unavailable and the run falls over to haiku, which then 400s on the un-clamped 128K max_tokens.

advisory.checklist_item: - [ ] Assert `settings['max_tokens'] == 128_000` for the unmapped-model case so the test detects a regression that clamps an unmapped model down to the 16000 default (mirror the sonnet positive control).
evidence: src/rebar/llm/config.py:117: `DEFAULT_MAX_TOKENS = 16000` — so fallback=16000 and the bound collapses to `<= 128000`
structured_run.py:287-290 source comment: clamping an unmapped model to the default 'would silently shrink a deliberate operator floor ... a regression worse than the bug' — the behavior under test

structured_run.py:291-293: for an unmapped model `_ceiling` is None so `eff_max_tokens` stays 128000; a regressed clamp to 16000 would still satisfy `<= 128000` and `> 0`, so the test cannot distinguish correct (128000) from regressed (16000) behavior
advisory.finding: test_an_unmapped_model_keeps_the_conservative_fallback is regression-blind for the exact anti-regression the change protects: it uses `assert settings['max_tokens'] <= max(fallback, 128_000)` (== `<= 128000` since fallback=16000). If the code wrongly clamped an unmapped model down to the 16000 default — precisely the mistake `_known_model_output_ceiling` is written to avoid — max_tokens would be 16000 and the assertion would still PASS. The test asserts too little to catch the operator-floor-shrinking regression its own docstring names.
advisory.suggested_fix: For non-empty unmapped models, assert `settings['max_tokens'] == 128_000` (the raised cap survives unclamped); the `None`/`""` cases will still hit the `not model` guard. Split the parametrization if the empty-model path needs a separate expectation.
